caveat: These meet the main-fabric rule, not a verified organic, untreated or plastic-free standard. Dyes, finishing chemistry and exact-product safety certificates remain unverified. No verified influencer endorsement of these brands was found.
evidenceNote: Influencer signal supports cotton/linen as a preference, not hormone or other health benefits. Grok returned sources before timing out; post text was checked via third-party mirrors. Community and long-term review coverage was not completed. Stock is storefront variant data, not an order guarantee. sources.title: AlpacaAurelius · fabric vs. finishes
sources.note: Warns that 100% cotton alone does not describe finishes and recommends organic natural clothing. His glyphosate statistic and blanket treatment/exposure claims are unverified. These budget picks are not established organic or untreated. Commercial supplement/coffee interests; clothing sponsorship unknown.

sources.title: DermNet · textile contact dermatitis
sources.type: Clinical education; not an exact-product test
sources.note: Identifies dyes, finishing resins, glues and nickel/elastic as possible contact allergens. For susceptible people recommends cotton/linen, loose fit, lighter colors and avoiding non-iron/dirt-repellent clothing. Dark/slim preferences are a trade-off if you have contact sensitivity; not proof dark pants are unsafe. No finish absence verified for these products.

sources.note: Tests against a defined harmful-substances standard; exact garment certificate and current scope matter. Not a zero-chemical or hormone-safety guarantee. No exact-product certificate established for this shortlist.
